treaty_name: Convention between the Government of Canada and the Government of the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1999)
eif_quote: Entry into Force 26 December 2000 | Justice Laws I-3.54: [Note: Convention and Protocol in force December 26, 2000, see Canada Gazette Part I, Volume 135, page 222.] | Art. 28(2)(a)(i): (i) in respect of tax withheld at the source on amounts paid or credited to non-residents, on or after the first day of January in the calendar year following that in which the Convention enters into force; and
source_title: Canada Treaty Information (GAC): Canada-Algeria Convention 1999 (E103143); Protocol in Income Tax Conventions Implementation Act, 1999, Schedule 3

rates.quote: 2. However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the dividends, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

2. However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the interest, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

2. However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the royalties, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.basis: none (MLI not in effect for this treaty)
ppt.quote: Algeria has signed the MLI (27-06-2024) but is not a Party, so the treaty is not a Covered Tax Agreement in effect (map.json).

notes: Flat 15% on dividends, interest and royalties. Not modelled: Art. 12(3) royalties for computer software or patents taxable only in residence State ("3. Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 2, royalties for the use of, or the right to use, computer software or any patent (but not including any such information provided in connection with a rental or franchise agreement), arising in a Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State who is the beneficial owner of the royalties shall be taxable only in that other State."); Art. 11(3) government/State-owned-institution and inter-governmental-framework loan interest exempt; Protocol para. 5: Algerian interest on EDC-guaranteed loans taxable only in Canada. Not MLI-covered (Algeria not a Party).
